items.title: [POC] implement a direct disk access queue to speed up persistent queue
items.body:
<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
This POC is a complete implementation of a queue backed by direct disk access.

It is made of 3 components:
* A queue interface similar to the storage interface for components to request Clients that allow access to the queue
* A change to the persistent queue to allow to use this interface (hacky workaround for now)
* A reference implementation that uses a set of rotating files to store queue data

<!-- Issue number if applicable -->
#### Link to tracking issue
Relates to #15384

<!--Describe what testing was performed and which tests were added.-->
#### Testing
Unit testing throughout - pardon the agentic mess. Also ran benchmarks.

<!--Describe the documentation added.-->
#### Documentation
Some documentation in code. We might like to add a few more README entries.

<!--Authorship attestation. See AGENTS.md for details. AI agents must not check this box on behalf
of the user; the human author must check it themselves before the PR is ready for review.-->
#### Authorship

- [x] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself.

<!--Please delete paragraphs that you did not use before submitting.-->


#### Performance benchmarks
I had Claude create a performance benchmark and compare to bbolt-backed file storage:

Here's the comparison, per 100 offer+consume operations (each b.Loop() iteration):


│ Queue │  ns/op  │  B/op │ allocs/op │
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
│ Memory                                           │ ~38,700        │ 4,900     │ 100       │
│ Persistent (mock/in-memory storage)              │ ~83,800        │ 96,800    │ 3,116     │
│ Disk (diskaccess extension, real files)          │ ~1,230,000     │ 15,130    │ 503       │
│ Persistent (real filestorage/bbolt, FSync: true) │ ~2,263,500,000 │ 8,175,000 │ 14,582    │


Takeaways:
  - With a real bbolt-backed filestorage extension and FSync: true, persistent queue drops from ~84µs/op to ~2.26 seconds/op — roughly 27,000x slower than the mock, and ~1,800x slower than the disk queue. This is fsync()-per-transaction cost: bbolt does a full durable commit (fsync + page writes) for every Batch call, and each Offer/consume does one.
  - Disk queue vs real filestorage is now the fair comparison you were after: disk queue (~1.23ms/op) is ~1,840x faster than fsync'd bbolt (~2,263ms/op) for the same 100-op batch, because diskaccess's writer only calls Sync() periodically (every SyncEvery writes / SyncTimeout tick) rather than fsync-ing on every single write like bbolt's transactional model does.

items.title: [pkg/exporterhelper] Keep the in-flight requests in the persistent queue when they fail during the shutdown
items.body:
<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description

The requests that failed while the collector was shutting down were deleted from the persistent queue instead of being redelivered after a restart. Only the retry sender reported such failures as shutdown errors, and only when a backoff wait was interrupted, so exporters that don't enable `retry_on_failure` always lost the requests that were in flight when the destination was unavailable. Requests that fail with a permanent error are still dropped.

<!-- Issue number if applicable -->
#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #15677 

<!--Describe what testing was performed and which tests were added.-->
#### Testing

Covered by added unit tests and I tested it with the elasticsearchexporter and confirms it resolves the issue in a persistent queue integration test.

items.title: [exporterhelper] keep queued items that fail during shutdown
items.body:
#### Description

So, our saving box (the persistent queue) is supposed to keep your data safe if things crash or restart. But we found a funny bug: if you turned the app off nicely (a clean shutdown), it accidentally threw all your saved data away! But if you yanked the power cord (a hard kill), it saved everything just fine. Weird, right?

That happened because it was looking at a specific, complicated error type to decide whether to save things or delete them.

Instead of guessing based on the error, I made it look at something it already knows (`pq.stopped`). Now, it knows for sure when we are shutting down and keeps your data safe no matter what.

#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #15677

#### Testing

I added two new tests in `persistent_queue_shutdown_loss_test.go` to make sure it's bulletproof:

Test 1: If a message fails while we're shutting down, it survives a restart. (This used to fail, but now it passes!)

Test 2: If a message successfully sends right as we're shutting down, it still gets deleted so we don't accidentally send it twice.

Everything in the exporter helper tree passes, and `make chlog-validate` is happy too.

#### Documentation

No documentation changes needed, but I added a little `.chloggen` entry (bug_fix, pkg/exporterhelper, issue 15677).

items.title: Fix shutdown deadlock caused by unbuffered async error channel
items.body:
### Summary
The Collector can **deadlock during shutdown** if a component reports a `StatusFatalError` while the shutdown sequence is already in progress.  
This happens because `asyncErrorChannel` is **unbuffered** and its **only receiver exits before shutdown begins**, causing a **blocking send** and an indefinite hang.

This PR fixes the issue by buffering `asyncErrorChannel` with capacity **1**, preserving existing behavior while guaranteeing shutdown never blocks.

---

### Problem Description

**Root cause**
- `asyncErrorChannel` is created as an **unbuffered channel**
- The main select loop (the only receiver) exits **before** `shutdown()` starts
- During shutdown, components may legally report `StatusFatalError`
- Reporting triggers a **blocking send** on `asyncErrorChannel`
- No receiver exists → **deadlock**

**Result**
- Collector hangs during shutdown
- Kubernetes pods remain stuck in `Terminating`
- Process is eventually SIGKILLed
- In-flight telemetry and persistent queues can be lost
- Failure is silent and hard to diagnose

---

### Reproduction Steps (Realistic)

1. Deploy the Collector in Kubernetes (DaemonSet or Deployment)
2. Configure an exporter (e.g. OTLP) with a persistent queue
3. Start sending telemetry traffic
4. Initiate a rolling restart (`kubectl rollout restart`)
5. Simultaneously make the exporter backend unreachable
6. Exporter reports `StatusFatalError` during shutdown
7. Observe the pod stuck in `Terminating` until SIGKILL

---

### Fix

```diff
- asyncErrorChannel: make(chan error),
+ asyncErrorChannel: make(chan error, 1),

items.title: Lifo Implementation of Caching fucntionality in Open-telemetry collector
items.body:
**Description**

Implemented LIFO caching semantics for the persistent exporter queue (the collector previously used FIFO behavior by default). This adds LIFO consumption while preserving sizing, in‑flight tracking, and dispatch behavior.

**Network Outage Simulation**

Simulated a network outage by stopping collector-2 (gRPC export target), sending bursts of MQTT messages to collector-1 (e.g., 3×300 via mosquitto_pub) so items are persisted to /var/lib/otelcol/throttle_storage, then restarting collector-2 and verifying the exported sequence in its logs to confirm LIFO ordering

**Changes Made**

[persistent_queue.go]:
Initialize lifoConsumeIndex from restored writeIndex on startup so LIFO consumption resumes correctly across restarts.
Persist the item key before updating writeIndex in putInternal to ensure crash-consistent write ordering.
Minor logging/comment clarifications.

**Manual testing**

Performed manual validation by sending 900 messages in 3 × 300 bursts (30s between bursts) while collector-2 was stopped, then started collector-2 to drain the persistent queue.
Observed behavior prior to automation: one anomalous first exported item (oldest), then strict LIFO ordering for the remaining items (e.g., 900 → 2). Changes address the ordering/pointer and write-ordering edge cases.

**Link to tracking Issue:**

items.title: [exporterhelper] Fix invalid write index updates in the persistent queue
items.body:
**Description:**
Fixing a bug where the in-memory value of the persistent queue's write index would be updated even if writing to the storage failed. This normally wouldn't have any negative effect other than inflating the queue size temporarily, as the read loop would simply skip over the nonexistent record. However, in the case where the storage doesn't have any available space, the in-memory and in-storage write index could become significantly different, at which point a collector restart would leave the queue in an inconsistent state.

Worth noting that the same issue affects reading from the queue, but in that case the writes are very small, and in practice the storage will almost always have enough space to carry them out.

**Link to tracking Issue:** #8115

**Testing:**
The `TestPersistentQueue_StorageFull` test actually only passed by accident. Writing would leave one additional item in the put channel, then the first read would fail (as there is not enough space to do the read index and dispatched items writes), but subsequent reads would succeed, so the bugs would cancel out. I modified this test to check for the number of items in the queue after inserting them, and also to expect one fewer item to be returned.

items.title: Propagate shutdown error from retry sender to fix data loss problem in persistent storage
items.body:
**Description:** <Describe what has changed. 
Fix a data loss bug occuring in persistent queue when otel collector restart.
When otel collector restart, the retry_sender will mark a request as finished and cause persistent storage to remove it from currentlyDispatchedItems. This causes data loss.

This change propagates an interrupted error when shutdown is called. The error propagates to the consumer callback function and each consumer can determine action against the error. The persistent storage is updated to check and ensure those requests are not marked as finished.

**Link to tracking Issue:** https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/6771

**Testing:**
- Added unit test around retry sender and persistent storage

**Documentation:**
Updated documentation for release note

items.title: [chore] [exporterhelper] Do not requeue on shutdown
items.body:
This change unblocks adding the `enqueue_on_failure` option to the queue sender by removing the requeue behavior on the shutdown. If we don't remove requeue on shutdown, it's possible to run into a situation described in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7388. After the recent refactoring, the chance of running into it is pretty small, but it's still possible.

The only reason to requeue on shutdown is to make sure there is no data loss with the persistent queue enabled. The persistent queue captures all the inflight requests in the persistent storage anyway, so there is no reason to requeue an inflight request. The only downside is it potentially can cause sending duplicate data on the collector restart in case of a partially failed request during shutdown.

Another option would be to rework the memory queue to never close the channel but still ensure draining.

items.title: Persistent storage in queued_retry, backed by file storage extension
items.body:
**Description:**

Persistent queue implementation within queued_retry, aimed at being compatible with Jager's [BoundedQueue](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/master/pkg/queue/bounded_queue.go) interface (providing a simple replacement) and backed by [file storage extension](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/extension/storage/filestorage) for storing WAL.

Currently, to run the persistent queue, OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib with `enable_unstable` build tag is required.

**Link to tracking Issue:** #2285 

[Design doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Y4vNthCGdYI61ezeAzL5dXWgiZ73y9eSjIDitk3zXsU/edit#)

**Testing:** Unit Tests and manual testing, more to come

**Documentation:** README.md updated, including an example

### [`v0.93.0`](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v0930)

##### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

-   `exporterhelper`: remove deprecated exporterhelper.RetrySettings and exporterhelper.NewDefaultRetrySettings ([#​9256](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9256))
-   `configopaque`: configopaque.String implements `fmt.Stringer` and `fmt.GoStringer`, outputting \[REDACTED] when formatted with the %s, %q or %#v verbs`(#​9213)
    This may break applications that rely on the previous behavior of opaque strings with`fmt.Sprintf`to e.g. build URLs or headers.
    Explicitly cast the opaque string to a string before using it in`fmt.Sprintf\` to restore the previous behavior.

##### 🚀 New components 🚀

-   `extension/memory_limiter`: Introduce a `memory_limiter` extension which receivers can use to reject incoming requests when collector doesn't have enough memory ([#​8632](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8632))
    The extension has the same configuration interface and behavior as the existing `memory_limiter` processor, which potentially can be deprecated and removed in the future

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

-   `configtls`: add `cipher_suites` to configtls. ([#​8105](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8105))
    Users can specify a list of cipher suites to pick from. If left blank, a safe default list is used.

-   `service`: mark `telemetry.useOtelForInternalMetrics` as stable ([#​816](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/816))

-   `exporters`: Cleanup log messages for export failures ([#​9219](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9219))
    1.  Ensure an error message is logged every time and only once when data is dropped/rejected due to export failure.
    2.  Update the wording. Specifically, don't use "dropped" term when an error is reported back to the pipeline.
        Keep the "dropped" wording for failures happened after the enabled queue.
    3.  Properly report any error reported by a queue. For example, a persistent storage error must be reported as a storage error, not as "queue overflow".

##### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

-   `configgrpc`: Update dependency to address a potential crash in the grpc instrumentation ([#​9296](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9296))
-   `otlpreceiver`: Ensure OTLP receiver handles consume errors correctly ([#​4335](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/4335))
    Make sure OTLP receiver returns correct status code and follows the receiver contract (gRPC)

##### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

-   `exporters/sending_queue`: Do not re-enqueue failed batches, rely on the retry_on_failure strategy instead. ([#​8382](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8382))
    The current re-enqueuing behavior is not obvious and cannot be configured. It takes place only for persistent queue
    and only if `retry_on_failure::enabled=true` even if `retry_on_failure` is a setting for a different backoff retry
    strategy. This change removes the re-enqueuing behavior. Consider increasing `retry_on_failure::max_elapsed_time`
    to reduce chances of data loss or set it to 0 to keep retrying until requests succeed.

-   `confmap`: Make the option `WithErrorUnused` enabled by default when unmarshaling configuration ([#​7102](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7102))
    The option `WithErrorUnused` is now enabled by default, and a new option `WithIgnoreUnused` is introduced to ignore
    errors about unused fields.

    This may break applications that rely on the previous behavior of opaque strings with`fmt.Sprintf`to e.g. build URLs or headers.
    Explicitly cast the opaque string to a string before using it in`fmt.Sprintf\` to restore the previous behavior.

##### 🚀 New components 🚀

    The extension has the same configuration interface and behavior as the existing `memory_limiter` processor, which potentially can be deprecated and removed in the future

    1.  Ensure an error message is logged every time and only once when data is dropped/rejected due to export failure.
    2.  Update the wording. Specifically, don't use "dropped" term when an error is reported back to the pipeline.
        Keep the "dropped" wording for failures happened after the enabled queue.
    3.  Properly report any error reported by a queue. For example, a persistent storage error must be reported as a storage error, not as "queue overflow".

##### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

    and only if `retry_on_failure::enabled=true` even if `retry_on_failure` is a setting for a different backoff retry
    strategy. This change removes the re-enqueuing behavior. Consider increasing `retry_on_failure::max_elapsed_time`
    to reduce chances of data loss or set it to 0 to keep retrying until requests succeed.

    This may break applications that rely on the previous behavior of opaque strings with`fmt.Sprintf`to e.g. build URLs or headers.
    Explicitly cast the opaque string to a string before using it in`fmt.Sprintf\` to restore the previous behavior.

##### 🚀 New components 🚀

-   `extension/memory_limiter`: Introduce a `memory_limiter` extension which receivers can use to reject incoming requests when collector doesn't have enough memory ([#​8632](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8632))
    The extension has the same configuration interface and behavior as the existing `memory_limiter` processor, which potentially can be deprecated and removed in the future

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

-   `configtls`: add `cipher_suites` to configtls. ([#​8105](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8105))
    Users can specify a list of cipher suites to pick from. If left blank, a safe default list is used.

-   `service`: mark `telemetry.useOtelForInternalMetrics` as stable ([#​816](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/816))

-   `exporters`: Cleanup log messages for export failures ([#​9219](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9219))
    1.  Ensure an error message is logged every time and only once when data is dropped/rejected due to export failure.
    2.  Update the wording. Specifically, don't use "dropped" term when an error is reported back to the pipeline.
        Keep the "dropped" wording for failures happened after the enabled queue.
    3.  Properly report any error reported by a queue. For example, a persistent storage error must be reported as a storage error, not as "queue overflow".

    This may break applications that rely on the previous behavior of opaque strings with`fmt.Sprintf`to e.g. build URLs or headers.
    Explicitly cast the opaque string to a string before using it in`fmt.Sprintf\` to restore the previous behavior.

    3.  Properly report any error reported by a queue. For example, a persistent storage error must be reported as a storage error, not as "queue overflow".

-   `configopaque`: configopaque.String implements `fmt.Stringer` and `fmt.GoStringer`, outputting \[REDACTED] when formatted with the %s, %q or %#v verbs`(#​9213)
    This may break applications that rely on the previous behavior of opaque strings with`fmt.Sprintf`to e.g. build URLs or headers.
    Explicitly cast the opaque string to a string before using it in`fmt.Sprintf\` to restore the previous behavior.

##### 🚀 New components 🚀

-   `extension/memory_limiter`: Introduce a `memory_limiter` extension which receivers can use to reject incoming requests when collector doesn't have enough memory ([#​8632](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8632))
    The extension has the same configuration interface and behavior as the existing `memory_limiter` processor, which potentially can be deprecated and removed in the future

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

-   `configtls`: add `cipher_suites` to configtls. ([#​8105](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8105))

-   `exporters`: Cleanup log messages for export failures ([#​9219](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9219))
    1.  Ensure an error message is logged every time and only once when data is dropped/rejected due to export failure.
    2.  Update the wording. Specifically, don't use "dropped" term when an error is reported back to the pipeline.
        Keep the "dropped" wording for failures happened after the enabled queue.
    3.  Properly report any error reported by a queue. For example, a persistent storage error must be reported as a storage error, not as "queue overflow".

##### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

-   `configgrpc`: Update dependency to address a potential crash in the grpc instrumentation ([#​9296](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9296))

    The current re-enqueuing behavior is not obvious and cannot be configured. It takes place only for persistent queue
    and only if `retry_on_failure::enabled=true` even if `retry_on_failure` is a setting for a different backoff retry
    strategy. This change removes the re-enqueuing behavior. Consider increasing `retry_on_failure::max_elapsed_time`
    to reduce chances of data loss or set it to 0 to keep retrying until requests succeed.

-   `confmap`: Make the option `WithErrorUnused` enabled by default when unmarshaling configuration ([#​7102](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7102))
    The option `WithErrorUnused` is now enabled by default, and a new option `WithIgnoreUnused` is introduced to ignore
    errors about unused fields.

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

    Validate that time.Duration, multiplier values in configretry are non-negative, and randomization_factor is between 0 and 1

-   `service`: Enable `telemetry.useOtelForInternalMetrics` by updating the flag to beta ([#​7454](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7454))
    The metrics generated should be consistent with the metrics generated
    previously with OpenCensus. Users can disable the behaviour
    by setting `--feature-gates -telemetry.useOtelForInternalMetrics` at

    -   Move the validation from start to the initialization phrase

-   `exporterhelper`: Add config Validate for TimeoutSettings ([#​9104](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9104))

##### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

-   `memorylimiterprocessor`: Fixed leaking goroutines from memorylimiterprocessor ([#​9099](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9099))
-   `cmd/otelcorecol`: Fix the code detecting if the collector is running as a service on Windows. ([#​7350](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7350))

### [`v0.93.0`](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v0930)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/compare/v0.92.0...v0.93.0)

##### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

-   `exporterhelper`: remove deprecated exporterhelper.RetrySettings and exporterhelper.NewDefaultRetrySettings ([#​9256](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9256))
-   `configopaque`: configopaque.String implements `fmt.Stringer` and `fmt.GoStringer`, outputting \[REDACTED] when formatted with the %s, %q or %#v verbs`(#​9213)
    This may break applications that rely on the previous behavior of opaque strings with`fmt.Sprintf`to e.g. build URLs or headers.
    Explicitly cast the opaque string to a string before using it in`fmt.Sprintf\` to restore the previous behavior.

##### 🚀 New components 🚀

-   `extension/memory_limiter`: Introduce a `memory_limiter` extension which receivers can use to reject incoming requests when collector doesn't have enough memory ([#​8632](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8632))
    The extension has the same configuration interface and behavior as the existing `memory_limiter` processor, which potentially can be deprecated and removed in the future

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

-   `configtls`: add `cipher_suites` to configtls. ([#​8105](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8105))
    Users can specify a list of cipher suites to pick from. If left blank, a safe default list is used.

-   `service`: mark `telemetry.useOtelForInternalMetrics` as stable ([#​816](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/816))

-   `exporters`: Cleanup log messages for export failures ([#​9219](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9219))
    1.  Ensure an error message is logged every time and only once when data is dropped/rejected due to export failure.
    2.  Update the wording. Specifically, don't use "dropped" term when an error is reported back to the pipeline.
        Keep the "dropped" wording for failures happened after the enabled queue.
    3.  Properly report any error reported by a queue. For example, a persistent storage error must be reported as a storage error, not as "queue overflow".

##### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

-   `configgrpc`: Update dependency to address a potential crash in the grpc instrumentation ([#​9296](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9296))
-   `otlpreceiver`: Ensure OTLP receiver handles consume errors correctly ([#​4335](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/4335))
    Make sure OTLP receiver returns correct status code and follows the receiver contract (gRPC)
-   `zpagesextension`: Remove mention of rpcz page from zpages extension ([#​9328](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9328))

### [`v0.92.0`](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v101v0920)

##### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

-   `exporters/sending_queue`: Do not re-enqueue failed batches, rely on the retry_on_failure strategy instead. ([#​8382](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8382))
    The current re-enqueuing behavior is not obvious and cannot be configured. It takes place only for persistent queue
    and only if `retry_on_failure::enabled=true` even if `retry_on_failure` is a setting for a different backoff retry
    strategy. This change removes the re-enqueuing behavior. Consider increasing `retry_on_failure::max_elapsed_time`
    to reduce chances of data loss or set it to 0 to keep retrying until requests succeed.

-   `confmap`: Make the option `WithErrorUnused` enabled by default when unmarshaling configuration ([#​7102](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7102))
    The option `WithErrorUnused` is now enabled by default, and a new option `WithIgnoreUnused` is introduced to ignore
    errors about unused fields.

-   `status`: Deprecate `ReportComponentStatus` in favor of `ReportStatus`. This new function does not return an error. ([#​9148](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/9148))

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector (go.opentelemetry.io/collector/service)</summary>

### [`v0.85.0`](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v0850)

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

-   `components command`: The "components" command now lists the component's stability levels. ([#​8289](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8289))
    Note that the format of this output is NOT stable and can change between versions.

-   `exporterhelper`: Stop logging error messages suggesting user to enable `retry_on_failure` or `sending_queue` when they are not available. ([#​8369](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8369))

### [`v0.84.0`](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v0840)

-   `service`: add OTLP export for internal traces ([#​8106](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8106))
-   `configgrpc`: Add support for :authority pseudo-header in grpc client ([#​8228](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8228))

##### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

### [`v0.83.0`](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v0830)

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

-   `extension`: Add optional `ConfigWatcher` interface ([#​6596](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/6596))
    Extensions implementing this interface will be notified of the Collector's effective config.

-   `otelcol`: Add optional `ConfmapProvider` interface for Config Providers ([#​6596](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/6596))
    This allows providing the Collector's configuration as a marshaled confmap.Conf object
    from a ConfigProvider

-   `service`: Add `CollectorConf` field to `service.Settings` ([#​6596](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/6596))
    This field is intended to be used by the Collector to pass its effective configuration to the service.

### [`v0.82.0`](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v100-rcv0014v0820)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/compare/v0.81.0...v0.82.0)

##### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

-   `service`: Enable configuration of collector telemetry through prometheus reader ([#​7641](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7641))
    These options are still experimental. To enable them, users must enable both
    `telemetry.useOtelForInternalMetrics` and `telemetry.useOtelWithSDKConfigurationForInternalTelemetry`
    feature gates. This change updates `metric_readers` to `readers` to align with the configuration
    working group.

-   `service`: Remove experimental `metric_readers.args` and `metric_reader.type` config options. ([#​7641](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7641))
    These options were experimental and did not have any effect on the configuration of
    the collector's telemetry. The change aligns the configuration with the latest iteration
    of the configuration json schema, which may still change in the future.

    These options are still experimental. To enable them, users must enable both
    `telemetry.useOtelForInternalMetrics` and `telemetry.useOtelWithSDKConfigurationForInternalTelemetry`
    feature gates. This change updates `metric_readers` to `readers` to align with the configuration
    working group.

-   `service`: Remove experimental `metric_readers.args` and `metric_reader.type` config options. ([#​7641](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7641))
    These options were experimental and did not have any effect on the configuration of
    the collector's telemetry. The change aligns the configuration with the latest iteration
    of the configuration json schema, which may still change in the future.

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

    These options are still experimental. To enable them, users must enable both
    `telemetry.useOtelForInternalMetrics` and `telemetry.useOtelWithSDKConfigurationForInternalTelemetry`
    feature gates.

-   `service`: Add support for OTLP export for internal metrics ([#​7641](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7641))
    Internal collector metrics can now be exported via OTLP
    using the otel-go otlpgrpc and otlphttp exporters.

-   `otlpreceiver`: Add http url paths per signal config options to otlpreceiver ([#​7511](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7511))

-   `otlphttpexporter`: Add support for trailing slash in endpoint URL ([#​8084](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/8084))
    URLs like `http://localhost:4318/` will now be treated as if they were `http://localhost:4318`

##### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

-   `connector`: Fix connector validation ([#​7892](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7892))
    Validation of connectors was too aggressive such that a connector that was used in any combination of unsupported roles would fail.
    Instead, validation should pass as long as each use of the connector has a supported corresponding use.

-   `scraperhelper`: Will start calling scrapers on component start. ([#​7635](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7635))

    -   Connectors connect pipelines by acting as an exporter in one or more pipelines and simultaneously
        as a receiver of corresponding data in one or more other pipelines. For example:
        -   The `forward` connector can export data to another pipeline of the same type. This allows you
            to merge data from multiple pipelines onto a common pipeline. Or, you can replicate data onto multiple
            pipelines so that it may be processed in different ways and/or exported to different backends.
        -   The `count` connector can count data of any type. Regardless of the type of data that is counted, it
            emits counts as metrics onto a metrics pipeline.

-   `otelcol`: Add connectors to output of the `components` command ([#​7809](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7809))

-   `scraperhelper`: Will start calling scrapers on component start. ([#​7635](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7635))
    The change allows scrapes to perform their initial scrape on component start
    and provide an initial delay. This means that scrapes will be delayed by `initial_delay`

-   `httpsprovider`: Add the httpsprovider. This component allows the collector to fetch configurations from web servers using the HTTPS protocol. ([#​6683](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/6683))

##### 💡 Enhancements 💡

-   `exporter`: Allow configuration of fields, `RandomizationFactor` and `Multiplier`, for exponential backoff algorithm when retry on failure is enabled ([#​6610](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/6610))
-   `connectors`: Add "connectors", a new type of pipeline component ([#​2336](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/2336))
    -   Connectors connect pipelines by acting as an exporter in one or more pipelines and simultaneously
        as a receiver of corresponding data in one or more other pipelines. For example:
        -   The `forward` connector can export data to another pipeline of the same type. This allows you
            to merge data from multiple pipelines onto a common pipeline. Or, you can replicate data onto multiple
            pipelines so that it may be processed in different ways and/or exported to different backends.
        -   The `count` connector can count data of any type. Regardless of the type of data that is counted, it
            emits counts as metrics onto a metrics pipeline.
    -   Connectors are currently disabled by default but can be enabled with the `service.connectors` feature gate.

-   `scraperhelper`: Will start calling scrapers on component start. ([#​7635](https://togithub.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/7635))
